key_insight: The paper shows that the linear Poisson source for wall-pressure fluctuations stays inner-scaled and approximately constant at very high Reynolds number, so it cannot explain the observed logarithmic growth in wall-pressure variance.
engineering_relevance: This isolates the growing wall-pressure variance to the nonlinear source, helping improve high-Reynolds-number turbulence models and wall-pressure predictions for aerodynamic and aeroacoustic design.
method: Used simultaneous velocity and velocity-gradient hot-wire measurements from Zimmermann et al. (2019).
Analyzed both a zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layer and a high-Reynolds-number pipe flow.
Tested inner-scaling collapse of the factors entering the linear pressure source up to friction Reynolds numbers of order 10^4.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the linear-source factors collapse across Reynolds number and that the relevant inertial-layer velocity-gradient variance decays inversely with wall distance.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on indirect source-term separation from measured statistics, so extending it to other wall-bounded flows or even higher Reynolds numbers should be done cautiously.
paper_title: An Inner-Scaled Linear Contribution to Wall-Pressure Variance at High Reynolds Number
